intended_object: According to its docstring, this is a helper for `Ordnode.findIndex`. It walks down a binary search tree while carrying an offset `i`. When it finds an element equivalent to `x` under `cmpLE`, it returns `i` plus that element's in-order index. If no such element exists, it returns `none`.
explanation: The docstring says outright that this is an auxiliary definition for `findIndex`. It is an accumulator-passing recursion that implements `findIndex` and has no counterpart in the mathematical literature. The recursion itself looks right. Going into the left subtree keeps the offset. A match returns the offset plus the size of the left subtree. Going into the right subtree adds the left subtree's size plus one. So it does give the in-order index shifted by `i`, which is what the helper is for. Still, it is an implementation detail, not a mathematical object.
